summary.text: The solubility pump is a physical and chemical process that carries carbon, as dissolved inorganic carbon, from the ocean's surface down into its interior.
Deep water forms under the same surface conditions that help carbon dioxide dissolve, so it holds more dissolved inorganic carbon than average surface water would suggest.
About one third of the carbon dioxide humans emit is thought to be entering the ocean today, and the solubility pump is the main mechanism behind that flow.

facts.label: Human CO₂ taken up
facts.value: About one third, roughly 2 gigatons of carbon yearly

facts.label: Route to the deep
facts.value: High-latitude deep water formation, especially the North Atlantic

facts.label: Predicted uptake ceiling
facts.value: About 5 gigatons of carbon per year by 2100

items.prompt: Carbon-rich deep water rises to the surface in warm waters near the equator. What happens to much of its carbon dioxide?

options.label: It stays dissolved and sinks back down
It escapes into the air above
It hardens into limestone on the seabed
It is locked into newly formed sea ice

items.explain: Warm water holds less carbon dioxide, so upwelling deep water near the equator releases the gas strongly to the atmosphere.

items.prompt: Climate change warms the ocean surface. How does this change the ocean's uptake of carbon dioxide from the air?

options.label: Uptake speeds up, since warm water mixes faster
Uptake stays the same, since temperature plays no part
Uptake slows, since warm water dissolves less CO₂
Uptake reverses at once, so the ocean only releases CO₂

items.explain: Warming lowers how much carbon dioxide seawater can dissolve, which slows the ocean's response to emissions.

items.prompt: Of all the carbon dioxide released by human activity, roughly what share is believed to be entering the ocean at present?

options.label: About one hundredth
About one tenth
Nearly all of it
About one third

items.explain: About one third of human CO₂ emissions, roughly 2 gigatons of carbon a year, is believed to be going into the ocean.

items.prompt: Carbon dioxide from burning fossil fuels dissolves into the sea. Through which kind of place does it mostly reach the deep ocean?

options.label: High-latitude sites where deep water forms
Warm equatorial waters where deep water rises
Shallow river mouths close to big cities
Hot springs that open on mid-ocean ridges

items.explain: Human-made CO₂ reaches the ocean interior through high-latitude sites of deep water formation, especially the North Atlantic.

items.prompt: The ocean keeps soaking up more and more carbon dioxide. What problem for sea creatures does this bring?

options.label: The water gets less salty
The water loses its dissolved nitrogen
The water freezes over more often
The water becomes more acidic

items.explain: Greater uptake of carbon dioxide leads to ocean acidification, which can cause trouble for marine life.

items.prompt: Suppose the ocean's slow overturning circulation weakened. What would that likely do to the movement of dissolved CO₂ into the deep ocean?

options.label: Reduce it
Increase it
Leave it unchanged
Move it into the air instead of the sea

items.explain: A slowing thermohaline circulation may cut how much dissolved CO₂ is carried into the deep ocean.
